title: Apparently this is a hot take- but I kind of liked Dog Day Afternoon?...
transcript: I actually think the critics were wrong about this one, because I saw Dog Day Afternoon on Broadway starring Jon Bernthal and Ebon Moss Bachrach, and I actually enjoyed it. I'm not gonna sit here and say that it is a perfect play by any stretch of the imagination, but you look at the review aggregates for the show, and it is, like, overwhelmingly negative. And I'm kind of surprised, because there is a lot to like here, most notably Jon Bernthal's central performance, which, to be fair, has been praised in pretty much every review I've read, and for good reason. Despite being billed as a double header between Jon and Ebon, this really is Jon's play. He absolutely carries this show and manages to bring a lot of humor, heart and sincerity. And the show is a lot funnier than I expected it to be for a play about a bank robbery. And from what I can gather, that seems to be the main critique that critics had, that the play leans too heavily into the comedy, that it kind of lessens the dramatic stakes. But honestly, I did still feel like there was sufficient tension to keep me engaged throughout. I do definitely think that there are some pacing issues, particularly when it comes to the ending. There's also a subplot with Jon Bernthal's wife that I didn't think was handled as well as it could have been, and it's introduced way too late in the show. To really make an impact. But I still left the theatre having enjoyed myself. And this is where I reveal that I haven't seen the movie that this play is based on, and based on what I've been hearing via word of mouth. That seems to be the main point of contention of people who liked the play and people who didn't, with people who have seen the movie feeling like the play isn't executed nearly as well. And while I think it is absolutely fair and valid to compare a play to its source material and how it chooses to adapt it, I do find it interesting that people who haven't seen the movie and are able to just judge the show purely on its own merits generally seem to be liking it. And because of that, I do have to argue that this play does stand on its own. Is it as good as the movie? Maybe not. Again, I haven't seen it. But divorced of that context, it works. It may not be perfect, but it works.
classificationReason: Creator states 'I saw Dog Day Afternoon on Broadway' (clear past-tense attendance), then shares detailed first-hand opinions on Jon Bernthal's performance, the comedy/drama balance, and pacing issues — a clear first-hand review.
